header.stance: 通膨與科技股降溫，實質殖利率卻上升

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價與晶片股下跌，美債仍續跌

週三原油下跌、歐洲通膨降溫、半導體股重挫，美債卻延續賣壓。10年期殖利率上升4個基點至4.48%，其中實質殖利率上升5個基點至2.25%，超過損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點至2.23%的幅度。30年期領跌，殖利率升至4.97%。

製造業仍在擴張，投入成本壓力則減輕。Fed主席Kevin Warsh也表示通膨風險已下降，一度使2年期殖利率觸及盤中低點；但他拒絕預告下一次決策，投資人仍須隨每項數據重新判斷利率路徑。當日通膨補償下降、各天期實質殖利率卻上升，市場討論因而集中在政策不確定性，而非能源衝擊重演。

這與週二的情況不同。前一天美債下跌伴隨股市強勢及職缺增加，週三半導體卻重挫6.27%，仍未帶來債券反彈。公司債基金也走弱，壽險資金卻繼續透過私募債支應大型AI項目。Brightline債權人協商與Trans-Oil債價急跌，則呈現基金報酬之外更大的個別差異。

## Warsh認為通膨風險降低，仍不預告利率決策

Warsh在辛特拉ECB論壇表示，過去四週通膨預期及風險已下降。2年期殖利率在發言期間降向4.15%，收盤卻回到4.17%，單日仍上升3個基點。5年期上升5個基點至4.24%，10年期升4個基點，30年期升6個基點。2年與10年期利差擴大1個基點至31，2年與30年期擴大3個基點至80。

其他天期實質殖利率也走高。5年及7年期各升5個基點至1.98%、2.11%；20年及30年期升4、5個基點至2.58%、2.78%。能源成本下降抑制通膨補償，卻未降低投資人持有美債所要求的實質報酬。

Warsh重申恢復物價穩定，但沒有說7月是否升息。FOMC 6月維持目標區間3.50%至3.75%，18份預測中有9份預期今年升息；Warsh確認自己是唯一未提交預測的官員。市場仍反映年底前至少升息25個基點。

減少政策指引的影響成為交易桌焦點。道明證券Gennadiy Goldberg與Molly Brooks認為，較少指引可能提高波動及期限溢價。他們統計6月會議後Fed公開露面12次，過去十年同期平均18次；美銀Mark Cabana也提到資訊減少與不確定性增加的取捨。不過，這仍是對未來的判斷，並非波動已明顯提高的證據。夏季發言本來就可能減少，地區聯準銀行總裁也未必改變原有頻率，一項常用債券波動指標在會議後仍相對穩定。

部位顯示，投資人一面看好美債，一面防範7月升息。交換價格反映約9個基點，相當於升息25個基點機率約36%；Warsh先前強調物價穩定以前，這項機率接近零。涵蓋7月29日決策的8月聯邦基金期貨，未平倉由6月會議前約45.4萬口升至週一近59萬口，增約30%。整體美債多頭部位同時達七個月最高，並有押注長端表現較佳的需求。短期政策避險與看多存續期間並存，並非所有部位都在表達相同利率預測。

### 製造業續擴張，成本升幅放緩

美國製造業連續第六個月擴張，ISM指標接近四年高點；美伊暫時協議壓低油價，投入價格指標則出現2022年7月以來最大月降幅。印刷、電氣設備、紡織等14個產業成長，紙製品、家具與木製品收縮。Raymond James經濟學家Eugenio Aleman認為，資料支持其今年經濟成長約2.4%的預測。

5月營建支出月增0.1%至年率$2.2102兆，仍比一年前少1.5%。住宅增加0.3%、公共工程增加0.5%，抵銷私人非住宅下降0.3%。紐約Fed勞動緊俏指數由修正後−0.07升至−0.02，離職及每名有效求職者對應職缺略增。其對應的三個月ECI薪資成長訊號為0.74%、年化2.96%，仍略低於標準化長期平均。活動維持韌性，並不代表薪資與投資全面加速。

多數短期國庫券上漲。4、6及8週期息票等值殖利率分別下降4、3及4個基點至3.63%、3.70%、3.69%；13週期降3個基點至3.80%，26週期降1個基點至3.97%。17及52週期則各升1個基點至3.89%、3.98%。

$720億119天期標售最高得標利率3.795%，投標倍數2.66，最高利率分配比例57.66%。間接投標人取得$388.38億，直接投標人$46.73億，主要交易商$268.69億。該券CUSIP為912797VP9，7月7日交割、11月3日到期，資金移轉將與後續短券一同落在假日之後。

## 壽險資金投入AI，困境債權人爭取控制權

截至5月，私募債發行約$810億，為2016年有紀錄以來同期最高。AI基礎設施吸引大額配置：IREN 5月發行約$21億，Blackstone支持的QTS已籌$8億，還計畫增加。壽險業去年年金銷售約$4,640億，長天期、高評級資產可配合其長期負債。

Broadcom與Anthropic基礎設施擴張的$350億融資，更顯示交易規模已擴大。它以傳統私募形式啟動，預計日後按Rule 144A交易。借款人可協商幣別、期限與結構，投資人則要求流動性較低的補償。這擴大了融資來源，也使更多AI曝險集中於透明度較低、條款日益複雜的證券。

Brightline有資金支付眼前票息，卻尚未解決$55億債務的未來安排。佛州鐵路的公司債及優先市政債7月1日付息，據報準備金足夠；持有$12億公司債多數部位的避險基金，仍準備拒絕不給予控制權的重整。為$11億免稅債提供保證的Assured Guaranty，已先提供短期營運貸款。

市政債權人考慮提供優先順位更高的融資，以取得股權，Fortress也準備交出控制權。各方希望先達成協議再聲請破產，減少訴訟成本，並避開鐵路破產涉及獨立受託人的特殊程序。預定付息所需現金與重整後誰掌握公司，是兩個不同問題；目前資訊並未證明票息已漏付。

### Trans-Oil遭指控拖累，Getty因贖回安排上漲

Trans-Oil $3億2031年債自週二開盤跌約21點至70美分附近，$4.5億2029年債也約70美分。烏克蘭媒體Ukrainska Pravda報導指控創辦股東Vaja Jhashi涉及違反制裁的對伊朗穀物運送，但報導未指名Trans-Oil公司本身。公司與Jhashi否認指控，並委託Pillsbury Winthrop Shaw Pittman律師事務所調查報導內容，安排週四英國夏令15:00召開投資人電話會議。

ING分析師Egor Fedorov預期對基本面影響有限，投資人仍尋求更多說明。2031年券5月15日還在面額附近，如今已明顯跌落。集團油籽加工業務遍及摩爾多瓦、羅馬尼亞與塞爾維亞，採購烏克蘭穀物，並在雷尼擁有兩座碼頭。相關指控仍有爭議，不能視為已確認的公司違規。

Getty Images宣布計畫終止收購Shutterstock、並贖回相關債券後，票息10.5%、2030年到期的$6.284億有擔保券上漲14美分至面額約98%。發行款一直存放在託管帳戶，等待監理批准。Getty也將大部分$3億2027年無擔保債展延一年，因此2028年前沒有到期債務；這批無擔保券不在贖回範圍，交易價格約為面額84%。兩者差異來自特定券種有託管款支應贖回，而非Getty整體信用改善。

歐洲不良債權供給也開始增加。APS Holding追蹤42個組合、面額€33億，高利率與德奧不動產壓力逐漸反映在銀行資產負債表。這為困境資產投資人帶來機會，也揭露了延後浮現的信用損失。

公司債基金同時面對指標殖利率與風險資產壓力：LQD跌0.56%至$108.46，HYG跌0.48%至$79.59，JNK跌0.51%至$95.88。大致同向的單日報酬，掩蓋了個別贖回、爭議新聞及重整協商間更大的差異。

紐約收盤後另有兩項融資消息。Clearlake旗下Tungsten Automation貸款由年初逾86美分跌至約61，貸款人已組成合作團體。信評機構指出流動性薄弱，循環與資產基礎融資使用增加，即使訂閱收入已占銷售90%也未消除疑慮。另一方面，海外發行人上半年袋鼠債達創紀錄的A$520億、約$360億，受惠亞洲需求及分散美元、歐元融資。跨境發債暢旺，與軟體借款人的債權人協調，是資金市場中截然不同的情況。

## 歐洲更有餘裕觀望，日本企業仍預期物價上升

歐元區6月通膨由3.2%降至2.8%，低於預估3.0%；核心降幅也超出預期，服務通膨降至3.2%。德國10年期殖利率收斂稍早升幅，但仍升2個基點至2.88%。資料提供支撐，卻未帶來德債全面反彈。

Christine Lagarde表示，油價回到戰前附近後，通膨上行與成長下行風險更趨平衡。Yannis Stournaras認為此次通膨大幅低於預期，除非情況劇變，7月幾乎沒有行動必要。Olli Rehn與Martin Kocher也認為近期第二輪風險下降；Ülo Kaasik仍覺得再升息一次合理，Philip Lane則強調薪資、食品與服務的延後反應。

ECB 6月升息後利率2.25%，預測仍顯示2027年相當一段時間通膨高於2%。7月行動可能性降低，9月取得更多薪資數據後，分歧可能更重要。當前能源降價與內部物價壓力能否持續消退，仍須分開判斷。

日本短觀在週三美國交易開始前已公布。大型製造商景氣由17升至22、為2018年以來最高；企業預期五年後年通膨2.6%，創2014年有資料以來最高。曾在日本央行編製短觀的岡三證券經濟學家Ko Nakayama表示，結果支持央行對通膨上行的擔憂。隔夜交換反映10月以前再升息機率58%。

稍晚報導日圓約162.73兌$1，市場質疑1%政策利率與逐步正常化，是否足以應對通膨、財政擴張及國際利差。一年期選擇權反映美元兌日圓觸及180的機率15%，屬極端情境，並非即將發生的預測。當局4月28日至5月27日已投入¥11.73兆，後續干預仍有可能。

貨幣基數資料則在美東19:50、紐約收盤後公布。6月年減13.7%，快於5月12.2%，日本央行往來帳戶餘額減少16.4%；季調月變化年化為下降22.9%。央行資產負債表流動性收縮，日圓弱勢卻持續增加政策利率上調壓力。

南韓數據也在稍後公布。6月整體通膨由3.1%升至3.2%，符合預期，核心維持2.5%。半導體出口近乎增至三倍，工作日調整後出口成長接近60%，使7月16日央行會議前還須考慮強勁需求。這些是下一個亞洲時段的更新；與較早的短觀不同，並非週三美國交易時已知的資料。

## 美元走強壓抑新興市場，印度更新債券流入紀錄

美國實質殖利率上升、美元指數漲0.20%至101.39，EMB跌0.44%至$96.02。新興市場匯率指標盤中跌0.2%，當時已回吐2026年漲幅。低油價減輕部分國家進口成本，仍不足以抵銷美元與資金外流壓力。

亞洲貨幣在Warsh發言前已轉弱。外資淨賣出₩1.46兆、約$9.38億南韓股票，韓元逼近2009年以來低點。稍後通膨報告又增加央行限制：即使匯率疲弱，物價壓力也使放鬆政策的空間有限。

印度較晚公布的6月資料顯示，完全開放管道政府債外資買進達4,180億盧比、約$44億，再創單月紀錄，延續減稅及擴大合格券後的買盤。10年期殖利率6月下降25個基點，為六年最大月降幅。澳盛經濟學家Dhiraj Nim除減稅外，也提到匯率穩定、升息預期延後及財政疑慮減輕。Pictet與Neuberger Berman考慮增持，M&G也轉趨正面。單月債券買進，與今年以來近$300億外資股票流出形成對比。

南非計畫增發既有蘭特計價伊斯蘭債券，支應會計年度籌資。約翰尼斯堡卻面對另一個問題：7月1日起的新年度估計有R21億預算缺口，尚無資金支應。國家財政部認為，相對查核結果，市府收入預測可能高估，應加強徵收與控制支出。國家仍可從本幣市場借款，並不能解決城市的收入短缺。

## 半導體重挫，未帶來美債避險買盤

費城半導體指數在強勁第二季後大跌6.27%，Nasdaq 100跌1.54%，S&P 500僅跌0.22%至7,483.23。VIX也只上升0.85%至16.59，仍比一週前低近11%。投資人重新評價AI漲勢中的集中部位，並未同等程度地反映全面股市衝擊。

WTI跌1.32%至$68.58，布蘭特跌1.85%至$71.57，兩者比一個月前低逾21%。美方形容與伊朗間接談判有建設性，荷莫茲海峽維持開放。EIA顯示截至6月26日當週商業原油庫存減少380萬桶、汽油減少230萬桶，仍未阻止期貨下跌；蒸餾油增加250萬桶，煉油使用率96.6%，戰略儲油則減少550萬桶。

黃金上漲1.13%至$4,068.30，月跌幅仍10.79%。美元走強與有限避險需求並行。債市最顯著的現象，是能源與晶片股都下跌，美債卻沒有上漲：實質殖利率提高，通膨補償降低。活動韌性與政策不確定性是合理解釋，但單日價格本身，無法證明期限溢價究竟增加多少。

## 非農與國庫券標售後，市場提早收盤

6月非農與截至6月27日當週失業救濟金，7月2日美東08:30公布，10:00接續5月工廠訂單。薪資、招聘及訂單可幫助判斷製造業韌性是否擴及其他部門。固定收益市場預定14:00收盤，調整部位的窗口較短；行情能否延續，比薄量時最初的殖利率變化更有參考價值。

財政部11:30標售4及8週期國庫券，各$850億，均在7月7日與週三$720億119天期交割。投標參與與交易商承接，將顯示近期上漲的短券能否消化集中資金需求；擔保融資利率則提供另一項觀察。

瑞士6月CPI美東02:30、歐元區5月失業率05:00公布，接續較低的歐元區通膨及內部物價持續性的討論。油價與美伊談判仍重要，勞動市場鬆緊及服務價格則決定，歐洲決策者能多大程度依靠能源降價帶來的緩解。
zh-TW.methodology_note: 除非另有註明，市場水準均以紐約收盤為基準。

overall_summary.headline: Warsh不預告利率決策，長天期美債續跌
overall_summary.session_narrative:
原油下跌、半導體股重挫6.27%，美債卻延續賣壓。2年期殖利率上升3個基點至4.17%，10年期上升4個基點至4.48%，30年期上升6個基點至4.97%。10年期實質殖利率增加5個基點，超過通膨補償下降1個基點的幅度。

Warsh表示通膨風險已減輕，卻不預告下一次利率決策。製造業續擴張、成本壓力下降；分析師擔心Fed減少溝通將增加不確定性，但債券波動尚未明顯改變。

壽險資金繼續承接大型AI私募債，Brightline債權人仍爭取控制權，Trans-Oil則因有爭議的指控跌價。歐元區通膨降至2.8%，較早公布的日本短觀卻顯示企業景氣與長期物價預期轉強。接下來是非農與國庫券標售，7月2日市場提早收盤。
overall_summary.summary: 10年期殖利率升至4.48%，實質殖利率提高、通膨補償下降。原油與半導體股走弱，30年期美債仍領跌。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Treasuries Keep Falling Despite Cheaper Oil and a Chip Rout

Treasuries extended their selloff Wednesday even as oil declined, European inflation cooled and semiconductor shares plunged. The 10-year yield rose 4 basis points to 4.48%; its real yield increased 5 to 2.25%, more than offsetting a 1-basis-point fall in breakeven inflation to 2.23%. The 30-year led the losses, taking its yield to 4.97%.

Manufacturing continued to expand, but input-cost pressure eased. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh also said inflation risks had diminished, briefly taking two-year yields to their intraday low. He declined to guide the next decision, however, leaving investors to reassess the path with each release. That uncertainty mattered more to the day's discussion than a renewed oil shock: inflation compensation fell while real yields rose across maturities.

The contrast with Tuesday was striking. That session's Treasury losses had accompanied strong equities and firm job openings; Wednesday brought a 6.27% semiconductor decline without a bond rally. Credit funds also fell, though insurers continued to finance large AI projects privately. Brightline's creditor negotiations and a sharp fall in Trans-Oil debt showed a much more uneven picture beneath the broad fund returns.

## Warsh Offers Inflation Relief, but No Rate Roadmap

Warsh told the ECB forum in Sintra that inflation expectations and risks had declined over the preceding four weeks. Two-year yields fell toward 4.15% during his remarks, then finished at 4.17%, up 3 basis points on the day. Five-year yields rose 5 basis points to 4.24%, the 10-year added 4 and the 30-year gained 6. The 2s10s spread widened 1 basis point to 31 and 2s30s widened 3 to 80.

Real yields rose beyond the benchmark maturity as well. Five- and seven-year yields each gained 5 basis points to 1.98% and 2.11%; 20- and 30-year yields increased 4 and 5 to 2.58% and 2.78%. Falling energy costs restrained the inflation component but did not reduce the real return investors demanded from Treasuries.

Warsh reiterated the commitment to price stability without saying whether July would bring an increase. The FOMC had held its target at 3.50%–3.75% in June; nine of the 18 submitted projections showed a hike this year. Warsh confirmed he alone had not submitted a projection. Investors still priced at least one quarter-point increase by year-end.

The prospect of less guidance was drawing attention on trading desks. TD Securities' Gennadiy Goldberg and Molly Brooks argued that reduced guidance could increase volatility and term premiums. They counted 12 public Fed appearances since the June meeting, compared with an average of 18 in the equivalent period over the preceding decade. BofA's Mark Cabana also highlighted the uncertainty trade-off. These were forecasts, not proof of a new volatility regime: summer communications often slow, regional presidents might maintain their usual schedules, and a widely followed bond-volatility gauge had been fairly steady since the meeting.

Positioning showed investors were preparing for a July increase even while favoring Treasuries more broadly. Swaps embedded about 9 basis points of a quarter-point hike, roughly a 36% probability, versus almost none before Warsh's earlier emphasis on price stability. Open interest in August fed-funds futures, which capture the July 29 decision, rose from about 454,000 contracts before the June meeting to nearly 590,000 by Monday, a gain of about 30%. Outright Treasury positioning was meanwhile the most bullish in seven months, with demand for long-end outperformance. Policy-risk hedges and a bullish duration view were coexisting, not expressing one uniform rate forecast.

### Factories Expand as Cost Pressure Eases

US manufacturing grew for a sixth consecutive month, with the ISM gauge near a four-year high. Its input-price measure recorded the largest monthly decline since July 2022 as the interim US-Iran agreement lowered oil prices. Fourteen industries reported growth, including printing, electrical equipment and textiles; paper, furniture and wood products contracted. Raymond James economist Eugenio Aleman said the report supported his forecast of roughly 2.4% growth this year.

May construction spending increased 0.1% to a $2.2102 trillion annual rate but remained 1.5% below a year earlier. Residential work rose 0.3% and public construction 0.5%, offsetting a 0.3% decline in private nonresidential activity. The New York Fed's labor-tightness index edged up to −0.02 from a revised −0.07 as quits and vacancies per effective searcher increased. Its associated three-month ECI wage-growth signal was 0.74%, or 2.96% annualized, still slightly below the normalized long-run mean. Activity was holding up without a uniformly stronger wage or investment picture.

Short bills rallied at most maturities. Four-, six- and eight-week coupon-equivalent yields fell 4, 3 and 4 basis points to 3.63%, 3.70% and 3.69%; 13 weeks declined 3 to 3.80%, and 26 weeks eased 1 to 3.97%. The exceptions were 17 and 52 weeks, each up 1 basis point to 3.89% and 3.98%.

The $72 billion 119-day auction stopped at 3.795%, with 2.66 bid-to-cover and 57.66% allotted at the high. Indirect bidders received $38.838 billion, direct bidders $4.673 billion and primary dealers $26.869 billion. The bill, CUSIP 912797VP9, settles July 7 and matures November 3. Its cash transfer lies beyond the holiday, alongside the next short-bill issues.

## Insurers Fund AI Projects as Creditors Contest Control

Private bond issuance reached about $81 billion through May, the highest for that period in records starting in 2016. AI infrastructure was drawing large allocations: IREN sold roughly $2.1 billion in May, and Blackstone-backed QTS had raised $800 million with plans for more. Life insurers could match long-dated, high-grade assets against annuity liabilities after industry annuity sales reached about $464 billion last year.

A $35 billion financing for Broadcom and Anthropic's infrastructure expansion illustrated how large the transactions had become. It began as a traditional private placement and was expected eventually to trade under Rule 144A. Negotiated currencies, maturities and structures gave borrowers flexibility, while investors sought compensation for illiquidity. The market expanded financing capacity but also concentrated more AI exposure in less transparent, increasingly complex securities.

Brightline's immediate coupon resources did not settle the future of its $5.5 billion debt burden. The Florida railway had corporate and senior municipal payments due July 1 and reportedly enough reserves to make them. Hedge funds controlling a majority of $1.2 billion of corporate debt were prepared to reject a restructuring that denied them control. Assured Guaranty, backing $1.1 billion of tax-exempt bonds, had supplied temporary operating loans.

Municipal creditors were considering super-senior financing that could give them ownership, while Fortress was prepared to relinquish control. Creditors sought agreement before filing to limit costs and avoid special railway bankruptcy procedures involving an independent trustee. Liquidity for the scheduled payment and an agreed allocation of control remained separate questions; the report did not establish a missed coupon.

### Allegations Hit Trans-Oil; an Escrow Redemption Lifts Getty

Trans-Oil's $300 million 2031 bond fell about 21 points from Tuesday's open to around 70 cents, where its $450 million 2029 issue was also quoted. A report by Ukrainska Pravda alleged that founding shareholder Vaja Jhashi was involved in sanctions-breaching grain shipments to Iran. The report did not name Trans-Oil itself. The company and Jhashi rejected the allegations, and the company hired Pillsbury Winthrop Shaw Pittman to investigate the reporting and scheduled an investor call for Thursday at 15:00 BST.

ING analyst Egor Fedorov expected limited impact on Trans-Oil's fundamentals. Investors were seeking further information while bonds traded far below par, which the 2031 issue had reached as recently as May 15. The group's oilseed operations span Moldova, Romania and Serbia, and it sources Ukrainian grain and owns two terminals in Reni. The allegations remained disputed rather than an established finding against the business.

Getty Images' $628.4 million 10.5% secured note due 2030 jumped 14 cents to about 98 after the company announced plans to terminate its Shutterstock acquisition and redeem the issue. Proceeds had remained in escrow pending regulatory approval. Getty had also extended most of a $300 million unsecured 2027 note by a year, leaving no maturity until 2028. Those unsecured notes traded around 84 and were not being redeemed. The divergence reflected the escrow-backed repayment of a particular issue, not a broad improvement in Getty's credit.

European distressed supply was also rebuilding. APS Holding was monitoring 42 non-performing-loan portfolios with €3.3 billion of face value as high rates and German and Austrian property stress reached bank balance sheets. Those sales offered new assets to distressed investors while exposing losses that had taken time to surface.

Corporate-bond funds fell with both benchmark yields and risk assets: LQD lost 0.56% to $108.46, HYG 0.48% to $79.59 and JNK 0.51% to $95.88. Their similar daily direction concealed the much larger divergence between redemptions, disputed headlines and restructuring negotiations.

Two later reports added fresh funding developments after New York closed. Lenders to Clearlake-backed Tungsten Automation formed a cooperation group as loans fell to about 61 cents from above 86 at the start of the year. Rating agencies cited thin liquidity and greater use of revolving and asset-based facilities despite subscription revenue reaching 90% of sales. Separately, overseas issuers sold a record A$52 billion, about $36 billion, of Kangaroo bonds in the first half, supported by Asian demand and diversification from dollars and euros. Strong cross-border issuance and creditor coordination around a strained software borrower were very different uses of the available capital.

## Europe Gains Room to Wait; Japan's Companies Expect Inflation

Euro-area June inflation slowed to 2.8% from 3.2%, below the 3.0% forecast. Core inflation also eased more than expected, and services inflation fell to 3.2%. German 10-year yields pared an earlier increase but still finished 2 basis points higher at 2.88%. The release offered relief without producing an outright Bund rally.

Christine Lagarde said upside inflation and downside growth risks had become more balanced as oil returned toward pre-war levels. Yannis Stournaras saw little reason for July action without a dramatic change after the large downside surprise. Olli Rehn and Martin Kocher also saw less immediate second-round risk. Ülo Kaasik still considered another increase reasonable, while Philip Lane emphasized delayed effects on wages, food and services.

June's increase had taken the ECB rate to 2.25%, and projections still put inflation above 2% well into 2027. With July action looking unlikely, the dispute could become more consequential in September after further wage data. Current energy relief and the persistence of domestic price pressure were not the same question.

Japan's Tankan, available before Wednesday's US trading session, showed large-manufacturer sentiment rising to 22 from 17, the strongest since 2018. Companies expected annual inflation of 2.6% five years ahead, a record in data back to 2014. Okasan Securities economist Ko Nakayama, a former BOJ compiler of the survey, said the result supported concern about upside inflation risks. Overnight swaps assigned a 58% probability to another BOJ increase by October.

Later reporting put the yen near 162.73 per dollar as investors questioned whether a 1% policy rate and gradual normalization were enough against inflation, fiscal expansion and the international rate gap. One-year options assigned a 15% probability to dollar-yen reaching 180, an extreme outcome rather than an imminent forecast. Intervention remained possible after authorities spent ¥11.73 trillion between April 28 and May 27.

The monetary-base release at 19:50 ET came after the completed New York close. June's base contracted 13.7% from a year earlier, faster than May's 12.2%, as BOJ current-account balances fell 16.4%. The seasonally adjusted monthly decline was 22.9% at an annualized rate. Balance-sheet liquidity was shrinking even as yen weakness sustained pressure for higher policy rates.

South Korean data also arrived later. June headline inflation rose to 3.2% from 3.1%, matching expectations, and core held at 2.5%. Semiconductor exports nearly tripled and working-day-adjusted export growth approached 60%, adding strong demand to the BOK's considerations before July 16. These updates mattered for the coming Asian session; unlike the earlier Tankan, they were not available during Wednesday's US trading.

## Dollar Strength Pressures EM as India Updates Its Inflow Record

EMB fell 0.44% to $96.02 as US real yields rose and DXY gained 0.20% to 101.39. An emerging-currency gauge lost 0.2% intraday, erasing its gain for 2026 at that point. Cheaper oil reduced import costs for some countries, but it did not prevent pressure from dollar strength and portfolio outflows.

Asian currencies weakened before Warsh's remarks. The won moved toward its weakest level since 2009 as foreigners sold a net ₩1.46 trillion, about $938 million, of Korean equities. The subsequent inflation report left the BOK with a further domestic constraint: price pressure limited room to ease even as the currency weakened.

India's later June tally put foreign purchases of fully accessible government bonds at a record 418 billion rupees, or $4.4 billion, following tax cuts and expanded eligibility. The 10-year yield fell 25 basis points during June, its largest monthly decline in six years. ANZ economist Dhiraj Nim cited currency stability, delayed hike expectations and receding fiscal concerns alongside the tax cuts. Pictet and Neuberger Berman were looking to add exposure, and M&G had turned more positive. The month's bond inflow contrasted with nearly $30 billion of foreign equity withdrawals over the year to date.

South Africa was planning to tap existing rand-denominated sukuk for fiscal-year funding. Johannesburg faced a different problem: an estimated R2.1 billion unfunded budget gap for the year starting July 1. National Treasury said the city's revenue projections appeared overstated against audited results and urged stronger collections and spending restraint. Access to national local-currency funding did not resolve the municipality's revenue shortfall.

## Semiconductors Slide Without a Treasury Haven Rally

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 6.27% after its strong second quarter. Nasdaq 100 fell 1.54%, while the S&P 500's decline was much smaller at 0.22%, to 7,483.23. VIX rose only 0.85% to 16.59 and remained almost 11% lower over a week. Investors marked down a concentrated part of the AI rally without pricing a comparably broad equity shock.

WTI fell 1.32% to $68.58 and Brent 1.85% to $71.57, both more than 21% below a month earlier. US officials described indirect Iran talks as constructive and Hormuz remained open. Futures declined despite the EIA reporting a 3.8 million-barrel commercial crude draw and a 2.3 million-barrel gasoline draw for the week ended June 26. Distillates rose 2.5 million barrels, refinery use reached 96.6% and the Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell 5.5 million barrels.

Gold gained 1.13% to $4,068.30, though it was still down 10.79% over the month. Dollar strength accompanied that limited demand for protection. The striking bond-market result was the absence of a rally alongside cheaper energy and falling chips: real yields rose while breakevens eased. Resilient activity and uncertainty about future policy remained plausible explanations; the daily moves alone could not establish how much additional term premium investors were demanding.

## Payrolls and Bill Auctions Precede the Early Close

June payrolls and claims for the week ended June 27 arrive July 2 at 08:30 ET, followed by May factory orders at 10:00. Wage growth, hiring and orders will help assess whether manufacturing's resilience extends further. The fixed-income session is scheduled to end at 14:00, giving investors a shorter window to adjust positions. A move that persists beyond the initial thin-market reaction would be more informative than the first yield change alone.

Treasury auctions $85 billion each of four- and eight-week bills at 11:30 ET. Both settle July 7, alongside Wednesday's $72 billion 119-day issue. Participation and dealer awards will show how demand for the recently rallying short maturities holds up against that concentrated cash transfer; secured funding rates provide a separate view of any collateral pressure.

Swiss June CPI is due at 02:30 ET and euro-area May unemployment at 05:00. They follow the softer euro-area inflation release and ongoing debate over domestic price persistence. Oil and US-Iran negotiations remain relevant, but labor slack and services prices will determine how much of the energy relief European policymakers can rely on.
